description: Team Nova is a youth-led innovation collective from Sri Lanka. We engineer accessible AI tools, gamified e-learning platforms, and zero-waste virtual STEM labs to empower secondary students and neurodivergent learners.
summary:
Outpost 89 is a browser-based 3D lunar survival and mission trainer that was created from the ground up using JavaScript, WebGL and Three.js. It takes space science and turns it into an exciting adventure. When we did a survey of than 50 students and found that 88.5% want to go to the Moon but 32.7% think it is a planet or a star we understood that just reading textbooks wasn't helping.

Outpost 89 directly answers the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. It places a custom 3D environment over NASA LRO elevation maps and LOLA data to create real lunar terrain and famous Apollo landing sites. Of just learning about space players experience 1/6th gravity look for water ice, study lunar minerals handle habitat life support move through Earth-to-Moon radio signal delays and talk to AI mission control voices.

We built this on low-spec PCs without any access to tools. We turned our challenges into our greatest strengths by using my younger brother’s fast creative ADHD brain to design optimized low-polygon 3D models and fun game features from scratch. The outcome is a lag-free lunar world that works on regular computers. It brings hands-on STEM education to students, in areas and encourages the next wave of astronauts."WHEN CHECKING THE GAME GOT TO THE GOOGLE DRIVE LINK DOWNLOAD AND CLICK THE HTML FILE"
details:
What does it do & how does it work? Web-based interactive 3D game: A fully interactive game that allows the user to play along with their lunar mission using an interactive 3D environment from within the browser. Real NASA Data: Custom made 3D environments are placed over real NASA data including LRO (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter) and LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) to create realistic lunar surfaces and Apollo landing sites. Interactive elements: This interactive game allows you to experience what it would really be like to be on the moon. You can feel the 1/6th gravity, manage your habitat systems, search for water ice and identify different minerals on the moon. You also have to deal with the long radio signals between earth and the moon along with dynamic mission control voices from AI.

Advantages of the project Easy to run on any computer: This has been designed to easily run on low spec computers so it can be used by rural and normal students who may not have high spec gaming equipment. Free to use: This has been created from scratch with no expensive game engines. Optimized: By using polygon optimization we have reduced the file size, memory usage and no lag.

Education Through Play: This helps children not get bored of learning from textbooks. They can experience 1/6th gravity, watch their oxygen levels drop and help bust some common myths about space. Encourages Questions: This helps encourage students to ask more questions. They can look at real craters on NASA and research for themselves. Encourages STEM Careers: This makes space science fun and encourages children to learn and pursue a career in aerospace and STEM. Learn about living on the moon: This teaches them practical skills about how humans can live, manage habitats and create sustainable settlements on the moon.

Technology, languages, software and equipment used JavaScript/WebGL/Three.js Data from real NASA LRO maps, LOLA data and AI. Low spec personal computers.

Creativity Combined Science & Myths: This has combined real NASA science with common lunar myths we found out from our surveys. Overcoming limitations: We had no high spec equipment or premium tools but we used our creativity to overcome this. One of our team members had a very quick and creative ADHD brain so we used this to our advantage to create an optimised, smooth and low poly interactive 3D world from scratch. Dynamic Voices & Footage: We have included dynamic voices from mission control (AI) and real historical footage from the moon landings.

Considerations & Challenges Survey: We did a survey before starting the project to gain insight. We found out that 88.5% of children think they will go to the moon in the future. 32.7% thought the moon was a planet/star and 7.7% thought it produced its own light. Low spec equipment: This was designed to work on low spec equipment. Optimised Polygons: We had to make sure we kept the number of polygons down to make sure there was no lag on standard computers. Real Data: We made sure our NASA data wasn’t just for show. We used real LOLA data to determine where the player could survive.
